chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام:
A man appointed two individuals as executors of his will. Is it permissible for one of them to act independently with half of the estate and the other with the other half?
So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: "It is not appropriate for them to go against the deceased, and they should act according to what he instructed them, if Allah wills."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: appointed through a will or bequest
key_terms.التَّرِكَةِ: the estate left behind by the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person whose instructions must be followed
key_terms.عَلَى حَسَبِ مَا أَمَرَهُمَا: in accordance with what he instructed them
key_terms.يُخَالِفَا الْمَيِّتَ: to act contrary to the deceased's instructions

ai.seo_question: When two executors are appointed in a will, can each one independently manage half of the estate?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about two executors appointed in a bequest. The Imam عليه السلام states that they are not to act contrary to the deceased's instructions, but must carry out the will in the manner he directed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5471 - Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Ṣaffar (may Allah (swt) be pleased with him) wrote to Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali Al-Askari (as) asking:
"A man appointed two individuals as executors of his will. Is it permissible for one of them to independently handle half of the inheritance and the other to manage the other half?"
Imam (as) responded in writing: "It is not appropriate for them to act contrary to the deceased's instructions. They should act according to what he commanded them, God willing."
